description: World runtime feel and presentation constants (docs/runtime/WORLD_RUNTIME.md). None of these is published by MeowDB: they are isometric-3D adaptation decisions, each with a reason. Read through WorldTuning; never duplicated in code.

ambient_neighbours.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.7.6: the presentation-only ambient layer for neighbouring hunting maps is milestone M3 and ships behind this flag; the World Review decides whether it stays on (open question 8). Not implemented (M3).

transition.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.5: a warp fades to black over 0.2 s and back over 0.2 s (whole warp <= 0.6 s); after the fade the player must be on the floor within 10 physics frames, and after 30 frames without floor the session re-places the player at player_spawns[0]. Gate commits blend camera bounds over 0.35 s; lighting/BGM crossfade over 0.5 s.

spawns.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE sections 4.5 and 4.7.1: a realize queues monster spawns nearest-first, at most 8 per frame, each fading in over 0.3 s; spawn slots stand at least 1.2 m apart and at least 4 m from every portal arrival. A slot first tries to land on its spawn area's own tier (within 0.6 m of the area's surface height), then on any walkable top surface in the area. Every slot stays inside the map's mob region, the layout footprint inset by 2 m (section 4.7.4); a map with MeowDB spawns but no exported spawn area samples that whole region (every map exports areas today). The clearance probe is 0.35 m in radius and as tall as the species' body (its canonical sprite height x WorldScale.actor when monsters/<id>.json fits the model to the sprite height), never shorter than 0.8 m, the old proxy approximation.

grounding.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE sections 4.9 and 4.13 (L1): a point counts as grounded when a ray from 1 m above to 3 m below hits walkable collision first, and the grounded point is within 0.3 m of that surface; a 0.3 x 1.5 m capsule lifted 0.05 m must be clear of blocking and containment collision. The capsule approximates the player body for static checks; the controller owns the real one (data/misostory/movement.json). A blocking surface lying within 0.05 m above walkable ground counts as that ground (interior floors carry a coplanar Walls slab 3 mm above Ground; Heena stands in her bush hull). When an arrival point or player spawn is not grounded or its capsule is blocked (a door mound, a hedge, a gate hull), the nearest grounded, clear point inside the map and outside every trigger is searched on rings up to 5 m around it in 0.5 m steps, inward first, and the move is logged as a warning (a Blender fix is the real cure).

containment.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.6: every map is walled by an invisible ring on the containment layer at footprint + 1.0 m (just outside the 1 m terrain overhang AUTHORING.md allows). The spec's '4 m tall' assumes flat maps; terraces rise up to ~10 m above a footprint's base_y, so each ring spans the map chunk's whole height (sidecar bounds) from 2 m below to 4 m above. Each trail end leaves a gap on the ring where its gate plane crosses it, as wide as the corridor between the trail's side walls (at most the gate width, portal_adaptations.json gates.half_width_m), so no slot opens beside a side wall; a plug body closes the gap while the link is in warp mode.

trails.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE sections 4.3 and 4.6. Trail side walls (containment layer, player only) follow the ribbon edges side_wall_offset_m outward, side_wall_height_m above the edge, from gate plane to gate plane; they reach side_wall_below_m under the edge because the trail flanks are walkable collision steeper than the 38 deg floor angle, so a player who got under a wall would slide off the island. A trail zone (RegionIndex) is the ribbon plus zone_margin_m, within zone_band_m of the centreline height. Until the export carries the centreline, the ribbon is derived from the trail mesh: its top is every face within top_max_slope_deg of level (Iteration One builds the top at 36 deg at most and the flanks at 49.6 deg or steeper).

region_invariant.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.3: ten times a second the player's last ground point must lie in current_map, a trail touching it, or the map of an armed gate. Five failing samples in a row push_error the position (dev and test builds fail on it; the traversal bot counts it); release builds also recover to SafeGround.

fall_recovery.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.6: an airborne player below kill_y (the lowest walkable height of the map minus 6 m; the sidecar's own kill_y when the exporter provides one) returns to the last SafeGround point with no damage, matching classic's lack of fall damage. A sea-level kill plane catches anything that leaves every map.

npc.reason: MeowDB documents no talk range (classic NPCs are clicked). The interact key talks to a current-map NPC within 1.6 m, a little more than the 1.5 m body height, so the player has to walk up to the NPC. Until the Blender export had markers for every MeowDB NPC (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 3.3: Todd, Sam, Mai), a missing one stood next to player_spawns[0], 2.5 m apart along the map frame, with a warning; the runtime keeps that fallback for future content.

session.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.9 step 4: a save naming an unknown map loads at 000000001 player_spawns[0] (the inferred start map, data/misostory/new_character.json). The saved location's resume point is refreshed from SafeGround four times a second so a save always carries a recent safe position.

environment.reason: Blender's sun strength (index.json environment, W/m^2) has no exact Godot equivalent; the Phase 1 probe matched the Blender look with energy = strength / pi (docs/runtime/blender_export.md, known issue 9). Per-map presets come from data/misostory/maps/<id>.json environment_preset; none differ yet.
